extracted_data.document_summary: This study, part of the Concussion Assessment, Research, and Education (CARE) Consortium, investigated the utility of plasma biomarkers (total tau, GFAP, and Nf-L) for predicting return-to-sport (RTS) duration following sport-related concussion (SRC) in collegiate athletes. It aimed to differentiate athletes returning to sport in less than 14 days versus 14 days or more post-injury. The findings indicated that higher total tau concentrations at 24-48 hours post-injury and at symptom resolution, and lower GFAP concentrations acutely post-injury, were associated with a protracted RTS (>=14 days). Nf-L was not significantly associated with RTS duration in this cohort.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of Sport-Related Concussion (SRC) recovery and return-to-sport (RTS) trajectories.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving 127 NCAA collegiate athletes who sustained an SRC. Plasma biomarker levels (total tau, GFAP, Nf-L) were measured at baseline, 0-21 hours, 24-48 hours post-injury, and at the time of symptom resolution. The study compared biomarker concentrations between athletes who returned to sport in less than 14 days versus those who took 14 days or more; no therapeutic interventions, specific doses, or dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: At 24-48 hours post-injury, mean plasma total tau was significantly higher in athletes with >=14 days RTS (-0.14 [0.14] pg/mL) compared to <14 days RTS (-0.65 [0.12] pg/mL) (P = .008). At symptom resolution, total tau showed acceptable discrimination power for RTS duration (AUC, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.63-0.86; P < .001). Baseline concentrations were not significantly different.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Microtubule-associated protein from neurons; an indicator of neuronal injury and recovery.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-Sport-Related Concussion (SRC) recovery monitoring in collegiate athletes, specifically measured at 24-48 hours post-injury and at the time of symptom resolution.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: May identify collegiate athletes who will require more time to Return-to-Sport (RTS) following SRC, indicating its utility in predicting longer recovery duration and tracking neuronal recovery.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Lower in athletes with protracted Return-to-Sport (RTS) (>=14 days) compared to those with shorter RTS (<14 days).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Acutely post-injury, mean plasma GFAP was 4.72 [0.12] pg/mL for the <14 days RTS group vs 4.39 [0.11] pg/mL for the >=14 days RTS group (P = .04). This implies lower GFAP in the longer RTS group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Released from astrocytes; an indicator of brain injury, potentially glial activation, commonly associated with more severe gradients of injury in mild Traumatic Brain Injury (mTBI).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Acutely post-Sport-Related Concussion (SRC) recovery monitoring in collegiate athletes, specifically comparing return to sport duration.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with RTS duration; lower levels were counterintuitively associated with protracted RTS in this cohort compared to prior mTBI studies, suggesting complex release kinetics or different injury characteristics in SRC. Its individual discriminatory power was not significant.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant difference in plasma Nf-L levels at 6 and 14 days post-SRC relative to baseline concentrations, and no significant associations with RTS duration after Bonferroni adjustment, despite a statistical interaction (F 1.9, 144.0 = 3.34; P = .04; p2 = 0.042).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects axonal damage due to injury or degeneration.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-Sport-Related Concussion (SRC) recovery monitoring in collegiate athletes.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Limited utility for discriminating or predicting RTS duration in this collegiate athlete SRC cohort due to lack of significant association and potentially limited sensitivity in milder cases.
